records.name: Capitolo Community Garden
records.summary: A community garden in Capitolo Playground at Tenth and Federal Streets, founded in 2009. It has 54 in-ground plots and three raised beds, and members share the garden's upkeep.
records.what_you_do: Members keep a plot, attend two workdays and two meetings each year, and take turns on shared chores such as watering the common beds and taking garden trash to the curb.

schedule.text: Two workdays and two meetings a year for members. The site does not list dates.

cost.text: No plot or membership fee is listed on the site.

first_step.how: Use the Join the Waitlist link on the How to Join page, or email capitologarden@gmail.com to ask about the waitlist
first_step.basis: Membership is open to anyone, but the plot waitlist is typically 3 to 4 years long.

records.notes: Status is probably_active because the home page welcomes members of the 2026 season, but that banner has no month, so last_sign_of_life is blank. The footer reads 2021. The Instagram link on the site points to a generic Wix page, so it was not recorded. Site address is the corner of Tenth and Federal Streets; City lists 900 Federal St. The waitlist sign-up is a Google form, which was not submitted.

records.name: Friends of Carpenter Green Park
records.summary: An all-volunteer nonprofit that looks after Carpenter Green Park in the Graduate Hospital area. Members help with daily upkeep, park events, and keeping the park safe and clean.
records.what_you_do: Members pay yearly dues and come to quarterly meetings. The group also holds park events and does upkeep work.

schedule.text: Quarterly meetings. The site lists no meeting dates or times. The park itself is open to the public.

cost.text: Annual membership is $20. Higher supporter levels cost more.

first_step.how: Email carpentergreenpark@gmail.com to get connected, and join for $20 a year
first_step.basis: Anyone can join, and the group says to email to get connected. The park itself is open to all.

records.notes: Status follows the newest dated item, an October 4, 2023 blog post. The home page describes membership and quarterly meetings as if current, so a visitor should confirm before going. City lists 920 S 17th St; the site gives 17th and Carpenter Streets. Footer reads 2021.

records.name: Friends of Carroll Park
records.summary: Neighbors who look after Carroll Park in West Philadelphia. The group began meeting in 2018 to join the City's Park Friends network, and in 2020 it ran programs and joined park cleanup days.
records.what_you_do: In 2020 the group ran socially distanced exercise sessions, shared census and voter registration information, and joined Love Your Park cleanup days.

first_step.how: Email carrollparkfriends@gmail.com and ask whether the group is still meeting

records.notes: Newest dated evidence found is a September 26, 2020 park field trip, reported in an October 2020 post. The group's Facebook page was not read, so it may be more active than we could check. The email is from the City list and was not verified. Carroll Park Neighbors (an older, separate group) is listed in leads_only.

records.name: Cedar Park Neighbors
records.summary: A community association for the Cedar Park neighborhood of West Philadelphia, open to households and businesses there. It holds public community meetings, runs committees such as parks and holiday baskets, and sends a weekly newsletter.
records.what_you_do: Members can vote in board elections and join a committee such as parks or transit. Board meetings are open to members, and the public part runs from 7 to 7:30 pm.

schedule.text: Public community meetings are held a few times a year (recent ones were September 16, 2025 and February 17, 2026). Board meetings are open to members.

cost.text: Membership starts at $10. Donations are tax-deductible.

first_step.how: Email secretary@cedarparkneighbors.org to ask how to join a committee or speak at the next public meeting
first_step.basis: The group says any neighbor can join, and it names committees and a contact page for newcomers.

records.notes: The group's own site is current, with its newest post dated June 2026. The events calendar did not load, so no upcoming dates are listed. The City list gives parks@cedarparkneighbors.org; the site publishes secretary@ instead, so the site address is used. The City lists it as a Friends group. The group calls itself a community association with a parks committee, so kind is civic.

records.name: Friends of Clark Park
records.summary: Neighbors who support Clark Park in West Philadelphia. They push for the park upgrades the City approved, such as nature-based playgrounds and a permanent restroom, and they host events such as Parktoberfest.
records.what_you_do: Join as a member or sign up to volunteer through the group's website. Members can also attend board meetings and events such as Parktoberfest.

schedule.text: Parktoberfest is Saturday, October 10, 2 to 8 pm. The page does not print the year, but October 10 is a Saturday in 2026. Board meeting dates are on a linked page and are not listed on the home page.

cost.text: Membership and donation amounts are not shown on the page.

first_step.how: Use the Volunteer page (friendsofclarkpark.org/volunteering) to sign up to help, or join at friendsofclarkpark.org/membership
first_step.basis: The membership and volunteer pages are public and say how to join. The site does not say beginners are welcome in so many words.

records.notes: Newest evidence is Parktoberfest, listed for Saturday October 10 with no year printed. The year 2026 is inferred from the weekday and from the home page's 'We Walk PHL Fall 2026' item, which does print the year. The calendar page lists no events and has a 2025 footer. The City lists 4301 Chester Ave; the site gives its address as 4300 to 4398 Baltimore Ave. The Instagram URL is built from the handle the site shows. Youth Soccer and other subpages were not read.

records.name: DC/AC Friends of Cliveden Park
records.summary: A Friends group for Cliveden Park in East Mount Airy. Volunteers took part in the citywide Love Your Park fall weekend in 2024, raking leaves, clearing litter, and mulching.
records.what_you_do: Helps with cleanup and planting work in the park, such as the 2024 Love Your Park fall weekend. We found no sign-up details.

first_step.how: Email Parks and Recreation's stewardship office (pprstewardship@phila.gov) and ask to be connected with this Friends group

records.notes: No own website found. The 6abc article (November 10, 2024) names Cliveden Park volunteers but not the Friends group, so the link to this group is an inference. A December 2019 awards post names Friends of Cliveden Park officers. The 2024 item is 23 months old, which is why status is probably_active. Do not confuse with the historic Cliveden house at 6401 Germantown Ave, a different organization. City address 501 E Johnson St; the 2024 article places the park in East Mount Airy. Audience open_to 'public' is assumed.

records.name: Friends of Cloverly Park
records.summary: Neighbors who care for Cloverly Park in Northwest Philadelphia. The group has worked on a tree care effort and on protecting the Old Tennis Court Farm. Past posts describe spring cleanups and plant sales.
records.what_you_do: Past posts describe spring cleanup days, community garden days, and plant sales at the Old Tennis Court Farm. The site's How can I help page lists ways to get involved; its contents were not checked.

schedule.text: Past events ran on Saturday mornings in spring and early summer, 10 am to 1 pm or 10 am to 2 pm. The site posts no current dates.

cost.text: No event price is posted. The site has a donate link with no amounts shown.

first_step.how: Email cloverlypark@yahoo.com and ask whether the group is still meeting and when its next cleanup is

records.notes: The newest dated item (July 4, 2025) is a City notice about a work stoppage, reposted on the group's news page, not a group event. The newest item the group wrote itself is a tree update from April 24, 2023. Read the status with that in mind. The City lists cloverlypark@yahoo.com; the site shows no email. The park address is from the City list; the site gives Wissahickon Avenue and School House Lane. Some linked pages were not read.

records.name: Cobbs Creek Ambassadors
records.summary: Volunteers who clean up and care for Cobbs Creek Park. They run registered cleanups, hand out plants, and host a summer festival at Whitby Park.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a cleanup through the group's registration link and meet the crew at the listed spot. Past cleanups collected anywhere from a few bags to 71 bags of litter.

schedule.text: Cleanups are posted on the group's cleanup calendar and open for registration; days and times vary. The summer festival was listed for Saturday, September 12, 2026, 11 am to 3 pm, at Whitby Park.

cost.text: Cleanup and festival costs are not listed.

first_step.how: Register for a cleanup through the Cleanup Registration link on cobbscreekparkambassadors.org, then show up at the listed spot
first_step.basis: Cleanups are posted publicly with a registration link, and the group invites volunteers.

records.notes: The festival date is listed on the site; whether it took place was not verified. The cleanup log's newest entry is November 2024, while the site's 2026 volunteer and trash totals are recent. Some January posts are labeled 2023 but sit among 2024 uploads. The site calls the group Cobbs Creek Park Ambassadors; the batch name is used. The email is from the City list and matches the site's calendar address. Festival partners (American Rivers, Audubon Society, Big Brothers Big Sisters, Clean Air Council) are organizations rather than neighborhood groups and were not checked.

records.name: Friends of Courtesy Stable
records.summary: A nonprofit that runs a riding stable near the Wissahickon in Fairmount Park, offering lessons, trail rides, and boarding. It also holds monthly volunteer days for park and barn upkeep.
records.what_you_do: Come to a monthly volunteer day to help with park and barn work, join the mailing list for volunteer openings, or take lessons and trail rides.

schedule.text: Monthly volunteer days, with no dates posted on the site. Lessons and rides are arranged by contacting the stable.

cost.text: Lesson, leasing, and boarding prices are not shown on the site.

first_step.how: Call the stable at 215-482-8108 and ask when the next monthly volunteer day is
first_step.basis: Volunteer days exist, but the site gives no dates and no sign-up steps, so the way in is unclear.

records.notes: The group's site calls it Boarders & Stewards of Courtesy Stable (BSCS). The City calls it Friends of Courtesy Stable, so the match uses the City record and the stable's address. It is mostly a riding facility; it is included because it is a nonprofit with a volunteer day program. The site has no dated items. Its copyright reads 2024, which is not evidence, and the status is probably_active under the working-site rule with no month. The City lists barnmanager@courtesystable.org, which the site does not show; the site's cynbarn0421@gmail.com is used. The City lists 8625 Wissahickon Ave (park address); the site's address is used.

notes: Batch file has no id field, so match.group_id is null throughout, as instructed. WebSearch cap of 3 reached (used on Carpenters Woods, Carroll Park and Cliveden); the six groups with no website or only a Facebook link (Campbell Square, Caseys Ice Pond, Centennial Lake, Cianfrani, Connell Park, Carpenters Woods) were not searched further. Facebook and Instagram pages were not read (platform rule). No 403 or bot checks were hit. Status counts: active 3 (Cedar Park Neighbors, Clark Park, Cobbs Creek Ambassadors), probably_active 4 (Capitolo, Cliveden, Cloverly, Courtesy Stable), dormant 2 (Carpenter Green Park, Carroll Park), unknown 6. Flag for the importer: Capitolo Community Garden and Friends of Courtesy Stable are probably_active on the brief's working-site rule, but have no month, so last_sign_of_life is null; the tier-1 field rule expects a value, so please decide whether to keep them. Cloverly's probably_active rests on a reposted City notice (July 2025), with the group's own last item from April 2023. The City's stewardship list page has no per-group entries; its only contact is the stewardship office, which was not used as a group contact. The Cliveden historic house (6401 Germantown Ave) is a different organization and was not used. Partners named on the Cobbs Creek festival page (American Rivers, Audubon Society, Big Brothers Big Sisters, Clean Air Council) are organizations rather than neighborhood groups, and no URLs were taken from that page, so they were not checked.
